column1: # Alerts ZAP raises that we keep ON PURPOSE. Read by .zap/summarize.py: an alert listed here is
# left out of the counts in the public step summary and listed underneath with its reason, and it
# stays in ZAP's own report regardless (CI keeps no copy of that; deploy/zap-scan.sh's local one
# still has it). Nothing else is hidden, and nothing is hidden without a reason.
# One line per alert, four TAB-separated fields:
#     <alertRef or rule id>  IGNORE  <alert name as ZAP prints it>  <one-line reason>
# Use the alertRef (10055-6), not the rule id (10055), wherever ZAP gives one. 10055 is ONE rule
# that raises a dozen different CSP alerts, and ignoring the rule would also hide the one that
# matters most here: script-src 'unsafe-inline' coming back (5b9b71f removed it).

column4: Kept on purpose on both apps: the tool's pages set about 41 inline styles through innerHTML (5b9b71f) and the portal's pages carry inline style attributes. script-src unsafe-inline is allowed on neither and still counts.
